persons.name: Heisenberg
persons.digest: On **BIST**, Heisenberg is on the defensive: he reminds followers he bought and sold at 270 in dollar terms, that price cannot get through the 200-week moving average, and that a failure there could take it to the 210-230 dollar zone. He treats BIST as a tactical trade, buying in tranches at support and selling at resistance, not a long-term story; about 90% of his portfolio is in foreign assets and even wiping out his Turkish stocks would cost 6-7% of the total. He also argues, citing SEC cases, that US markets are not free of fraud and manipulation, and shares a report of Brazil's stock market opening down 19.5%.

persons.name: Ahmet Sunelcan
persons.digest: Ahmet Sunelcan wrote that he closed his **CRWV** short at a small profit. His main long post is on Nvidia lowering the Rubin HBM4 speed requirement from 11.7 Gbps to 9.6 Gbps: per-GPU bandwidth drops from ~22 TB/s to ~19.7 TB/s, a loss of roughly 10-11% in memory-bound inference. In his view this is relief on volume and qualification for **SK hynix** and **Micron**, while the value of Samsung's speed advantage shrinks; **AMD MI450**'s reported bandwidth is still ahead.

items.title: Rubin HBM4 speed requirement cut to 9.6 Gbps
items.summary: Pin speed falls from 11.7 to 9.6 Gbps (~18%) and per-GPU bandwidth from ~22 to ~19.7 TB/s, a ~10-11% loss in memory-bound inference. 9.6 Gbps is the top of the JEDEC HBM4 range and all three makers can hit it comfortably. It is relief for SK hynix and Micron, while the value of Samsung's speed lead shrinks; AMD MI450's 23.3 TB/s is still ahead.

assets.note: Relief on volume and qualification.
